author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Rye voters approved two ballot measures that point in different directions for a migratory colony of barn swallows at the town-owned Goss Barn, leaving local officials to determine how the results can be carried out together.

A warrant article calling for the historic barn to remain a wildlife-free municipal building in perpetuity passed 1,248 to 1,113, according to New Hampshire Public Radio. A separate measure barring officials from disturbing bird colonies on town land unless the birds pose a public-health risk passed 1,232 to 1,122.

Barn swallows have nested at the site for decades. The dispute sharpened after concerns about droppings led the town to seal the barn and spend about $13,000 on cleaning. Public meetings and a lawsuit have already made the issue one of Rye’s most closely watched local debates.

Town Administrator Matt Scruton said the town would review the language and determine its next steps. The Rye Conservation Commission is scheduled to meet Thursday, when members are expected to examine the overlapping instructions. Any resolution will have to account for the votes, the building’s municipal use and the circumstances under which the public-health exception could apply.
dek: One measure calls for the town-owned barn to remain wildlife-free, while another restricts officials from disturbing bird colonies.
headline: Rye voters approve conflicting rules for Goss Barn swallows
